exposure: serum progesterone concentration in early pregnancy
outcome: risk of preterm delivery (any and spontaneous)
cohort: The study included 1860 mother-newborn pairs from the Born in Guangzhou Cohort Study, consisting of women with singleton pregnancies who had serum progesterone measured between 4 and 10 weeks of gestation.
finding: Lower first trimester serum progesterone concentration was not associated with a reduction in the length of gestation or an increased risk of preterm delivery.
gest_age: Exposure measured between 4 and 10 weeks of gestation; outcomes related to duration of pregnancy and preterm delivery.
